reason: The text explicitly depicts Yahweh as both remote and all-powerful. Remoteness is demonstrated through: (1) the command that people worship 'from a distance' (מֵרָחֹק), (2) strict boundaries preventing approach to Mount Sinai with threat of death, (3) only Moses permitted direct approach to Yahweh, and (4) the requirement that the people maintain separation. All-powerful attributes are evident through: (1) Yahweh's dramatic descent visible to all people on the mountain, (2) the lethal danger of touching the mountain (death by stoning or arrows), (3) warnings of Yahweh 'breaking out' destructively against the people, and (4) Yahweh's direct commands controlling all actions and preparations. The text presents a God who maintains authoritative distance while demonstrating overwhelming divine power.
